{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZisP2Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDJemk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 67, "title": "Implement V30MZ vector-1 single-step delivery and trap-aware CPU regressions", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `6cabc27cafb174fc0d08b7d0cb750d0249f2de89`, `Cpu::step` never generates vector 1. TF is writable and cleared during interrupt entry, but otherwise remains inert. Software enabling single-step therefore continues without its handler.

Static reproduction, not executed during planning: install vector 1, execute `POPF; NOP; MOV BX,1234` at CS:IP `0000:1000`, and restore FLAGS=F102. Current code reaches MOV without trapping. Expected delivery occurs after NOP, before MOV, with saved IP=1002, CS=0000 and FLAGS=F102; handler FLAGS have IF/TF cleared.

Existing tests depend on the omission. For example, `cpu/divide_tests.rs` restores FFD7 with POPF and executes NOP and further instructions without a handler. Implementing delivery requires preserving their arithmetic and multiplication-history assertions through valid trap-aware observations. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

Implement source-grounded vector-1 delivery through ordinary CPU execution, including activation, entry, continuation, suppression boundaries and interaction with existing interrupts/device scheduling. Apply it across emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations independently of supported graphics modes.

Keep this task focused on single-step behavior and necessary cross-file regressions. Exceptional division continuation, REP on non-string instructions, new NMI sources, prefetch and general timing accuracy remain separate work.

## Context

The clean local checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. GitHub’s open collection is empty; all 66 closed Issue/PR titles were checked. [Issue #65](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/65) explicitly deferred single-step delivery.

The [NEC V30MZ hardware manual, chapter 5](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary) specifies vector-1 activation, interrupt entry, priority and excluded boundaries. SS loads defer single-step; segment/repeat/BUSLOCK prefixes cannot be separated from their instruction. IF-enabling delays are specifically for external INT. Its block-interruption section describes hardware interrupts, so it must not alone establish TF cadence within REP.

Independent [interrupt experiments](https://github.com/asiekierka/ws-test-suite/blob/5d8950d6b271a585c252af3ced93fbd2045f4752/src/mono/cpu/interrupt_timing/tests.s) place the expected saved IP after POPF+NOP and POPF+STI. The [companion harness](https://github.com/asiekierka/ws-test-suite/blob/5d8950d6b271a585c252af3ced93fbd2045f4752/src/mono/cpu/interrupt_timing/main.c) compares against separate labels. These are inspected experiment sources, not observed console passes.

Bounded prerequisite within this task: before changing REP/HALT handling or assigning trap-entry clocks, record independent expected traces and accounting. Reconcile the V30MZ manual with the [related NEC instruction manual](https://datasheets.chipdb.org/NEC/V20-V30/U11301EJ5V0UMJ1.PDF) and inspected [ares dispatch](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/c76aaffa6e69778baf9a66d1da04298ac2ed7d1d/ares/component/processor/v30mz/instruction.cpp) and string handling. Distinguish direct requirements from integration inferences; older-core rules and upstream implementation are not console measurements. Cover REP element/final/zero-count boundaries and TF+HLT explicitly rather than equating a host `step` call with a completed instruction. Resolve this through source reasoning and automated vectors without a human gate.

Correction record: old assumption—TF may remain set while subsequent instructions execute indefinitely without delivery. Corrected requirement—deliver the architectural trap at applicable boundaries and inspect saved FLAGS when entry clears live flags. Rationale: the primary manual and independent POPF/STI vectors contradict inert TF. Preserve prior valid arithmetic/control-flag acceptance; record further evidence-based corrections without human approval or independent AI re-review.

[Saved #65 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/6cabc27cafb174fc0d08b7d0cb750d0249f2de89/docs/issue-65-validation.md) reports 215 workspace tests and complete production Chromium suites passing. Tests are present and those passes are reported; no builds/tests were run during this planning inspection.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the source reconciliation, REP/HALT boundary traces and trap-entry accounting before implementing those paths. Specify observable saved IP/CS/FLAGS, register progress and delivery order independently of production helpers. Retain explicit uncertainty about exact silicon phases.
- [ ] Implement vector-1 entry and POPF/IRET activation. Add the literal reproduction above, IF-clear/set cases, repeated stepping after IRET, and handler clearing of stacked TF to stop stepping. Assert stack order, normalized FLAGS, SP, continuation and absence of unintended handler recursion.
- [ ] Cover MOV SS from register/memory, POP SS, negative controls using other segment operations, segment/BUSLOCK/repeat prefixes and mixed prefixes. Reproduce the independent POPF+NOP and POPF+STI saved-IP expectations. Keep single-step suppression distinct from the existing external-IRQ shadow.
- [ ] Add independent traces for eligible simultaneous IRQs and existing synchronous interrupts, checking priority, selected vector, saved state and return behavior without fabricated nested traps. Exercise the reconciled REP/HALT cases, including remaining count, prefix restart and no skipped/duplicated elements. DMA-only stalls and sustained HALT idle calls must not count as newly executed instructions.
- [ ] Preserve multiplication history and every valid arithmetic result/full-FLAGS/branch assertion. Replace inert-TF assumptions with handlers, saved-frame observations or carefully isolated single-instruction checks; retain explicit TF coverage. Preserve existing division-fault requirements unless separately corrected by recorded primary evidence.
- [ ] Cover all three emulated model configurations, every supported graphics mode and runtime transitions. Check trap-state cloning and isolation across reset/restart, successful replacement/model changes, and rejected lifecycle operations. Through normal Machine scheduling, verify instruction, trap and DMA costs advance timers, raster/frame and audio once without executing an extra application instruction.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 trap fixture using existing fixture tooling. Native integration and production Chromium/Wasm checks must compare CPU-written handler counts, saved frames and continuation markers against independent expectations on every model and fresh restart. Poison stale observations and invalidate completion. Record an actual pre-fix focused native failure and native fixture failure, then corrected passes.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview. Preserve model gates, firmware-free startup, video/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/EEPROM/RTC retention, browser save integrity and ownership/provenance.
- [ ] Update hardware-support, source-reconciliation and fixture-provenance documentation. Record final source/fixture identities, actual commands/results, failures/resolutions and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox and resolves blocking findings before merge. Original probe passes must not be reported as commercial-game readiness.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-browser discrimination, additional browser engines and additional lawfully available software. Physical-console comparisons and human gameplay are optional and were unperformed during planning. No proprietary ROM or firmware is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
